title: Polymorphic stream consumer: unified async-iterable and Web Stream adapter for TS SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a small, well-documented polymorphic consumer in the TypeScript SDK that accepts generation responses as either an AsyncIterable (for for-await-of) or a ReadableStream/Web Stream (for browser/WHATWG streams), with consistent cancellation, backpressure, and retry semantics.

Why: Teams keep implementing ad-hoc bridges between AsyncIterable and Web Streams; subtle differences in cancellation, error propagation, and chunk framing cause bugs (leaked timers, double-close, non-idempotent retries). A single, SDK-maintained consumer reduces duplicate code, improves ergonomics, and standardizes correctness.

Scope (MVP):
- Export a PolymorphicConsumer factory: accepts input of type AsyncIterable<Bytes|Token|Chunk> | ReadableStream<Bytes|Chunk> and returns a unified AsyncIterable<Chunk> and an optional ReadableStream<Chunk> view.
- Correct cancellation semantics: consumer.signal.abort() should cancel underlying network request and close both views.
- Backpressure: when consuming as Web Stream, use Built-in backpressure from Writable stream; when consuming as AsyncIterable, apply a small in-memory queue with configurable high-water mark.
- Retries: surface a retry hook that receives last-successful-sequence-id so network layer can resume safely for resumable streams.
- Examples: two short snippets (for-await-of and piping to a browser writable).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Implementation uses a single source dispatcher that reads from network sockets and enqueues framed chunks. To avoid duplication we create a lightweight ReadableStream from the same queue (reader/writer pair). The AsyncIterable pulls from the same queue. This keeps ordering identical.
- We avoid converting ReadableStream into AsyncIterable via for-await-of on the stream reader because that approach hides backpressure differences and complicates cancellation propagation. The chosen design explicitly ties stream cancellation to the underlying AbortController.
- Memory vs latency: default HWM=16 chunks. Larger values reduce network round-trips for small bursts but increase memory. Exposed as option.
- Retry strategy: only support resumable streams that expose a server-side resume token. Client exposes onProgress(token) callback; the retry logic is pluggable. Non-resumable streams will not be retried by default.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests validating: (1) cancellation cancels network request and both views close; (2) ordering identical across both views; (3) backpressure honors HighWaterMark config; (4) resume-token passed to retry hook on transient network failure.
- Integration example added to docs and a small E2E in examples/ts/stream-polymorphic.ts.
- API surface minimal and documented in SDK changelog.

Example usage (sketch):
// for-await-of consumer
const consumer = PolymorphicConsumer.from(responseStream, {highWaterMark: 32});
for await (const chunk of consumer.iterable) {
  console.log(chunk.text);
}

// browser pipe consumer
const consumer = PolymorphicConsumer.from(responseStream);
const writable = new WritableStream({write(chunk){ /* render DOM */ }});
await consumer.stream.pipeTo(writable);

comments: 2025-02-11 | Asha Patel: Spiked two prototypes. One uses ReadableStreamDefaultController + shared queue, the other folds everything into an async generator that exposes a createReadableStream() helper. The shared-queue controller feels more explicit for backpressure and is easier to tie to AbortController.

2025-02-14 | Marco Nguyen: Reviewed prototype; requested clear API for retry hook and default HWM. Also flagged we should avoid adding heavy dependencies. Recommend keeping implementation small and isolated in packages/sdk/ts/stream-utils.
2025-02-20 | SRE - Jaime Ortiz: Run manual stress test against dev runtime. Observed no memory growth for HWM <= 128 across 10k short-lived requests. Added note to README about default HWM tradeoffs.
